## Summary

`scripts/mutation_gate.py` isolates the **source tree** (`git archive` into a temp
dir) but not **runtime effects**: `execute_shard()` (line 563) runs pytest as a
subprocess against the real filesystem. On 2026-08-26 a mutation removed a guard from
a shell script that performs real deletion, a test exec'd that script with an empty
path variable, and the glob expanded to `rm -rf /*` — destroying `/opt/homebrew` and
every Homebrew-installed app in `/Applications` on a contributor workstation. Only a
60-second subprocess timeout stopped it; `/Users` was still ahead of it in the target
list.

## Why source-tree isolation was never going to help

Researched across the major tools — cargo-mutants, mutmut, StrykerJS, PIT, mull.
**Every one isolates the source tree; none isolates runtime effects.** A copied tree
does nothing when the mutated code calls `rm -rf /` — the syscall still lands.
cargo-mutants documents this hazard explicitly
(https://mutants.rs/cautions.html): *"it might modify existing deletion paths in your
code… could potentially delete unintended directories… Run in an isolated environment
(container, CI, or VM)."* No mutation tool in any language ships OS-level sandboxing;
it is the caller's job.

## Why guards inside the script are not enough

The harness string-substitutes the artifact under test, so **any guard expressed in
that artifact can be deleted by a mutation** — including `${dir:?}`. `${dir:?}` is
worth adding (statement-removal operators, the most common kind, won't naturally
rewrite an `rm` argument), but it is hardening, not a control. **Only a layer outside
the mutated artifact is load-bearing.** That is this ticket.

Note also that `set -euo pipefail` would NOT have fired: `set -u` triggers on *unset*,
not set-but-empty, and the variable was `""`. Verified.

## Scope

1. **Sandbox the mutation run** — the load-bearing control.
2. **A durable guard against destructive test-exec** — the general form of "the test
   should never have been able to delete anything". The specific offending test is not
   on `main` (it lives on the unmerged `fix-mcp-clone-blocks-boot` branch), so a
   one-file fix has nothing to attach to here; a lint gate in the existing
   `scripts/check_*.py` family generalizes it and catches the next one.

Out of scope: hardening `mcp-entrypoint.sh` itself (`${dir:?}` + deny-list) — that
file exists only on the unmerged branch and belongs with Gerrit change 2244.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `execute_shard()` runs its pytest subprocess inside an OS-enforced sandbox that
      denies filesystem writes outside an explicit allow-list (scratch tree, pytest
      basetemp, the venv, `/dev/null`). Verified by `pytest tests/unit/test_mutation_sandbox.py`.
- [ ] The sandbox is fail-closed: with no sandbox mechanism available the run ABORTS
      with an actionable message naming the opt-out. Verified by a test asserting a
      non-zero exit when the mechanism is stubbed absent.
- [ ] A documented opt-out env var waives the sandbox and logs at WARNING when used.
      A silent unsandboxed fallback is rejected. Verified by asserting the WARNING
      record is emitted.
- [ ] Portable per `project.portability`: the mechanism is an OS facility (macOS
      Seatbelt `sandbox-exec`; a Linux equivalent such as `bwrap`/`unshare`), never a
      CI-provider feature. Verified by running `make lint` and the sandbox test on a
      developer host with no CI involved.
- [ ] The sandbox demonstrably DENIES: a probe writing outside the allow-list under
      the wrapper exits non-zero and the file is absent; the same probe inside the
      allow-list succeeds. Asserting wrapper argv alone does not satisfy this — the
      test must observe enforcement.
- [ ] A lint gate flags a test that `subprocess`-execs a shell script containing an
      unguarded destructive deletion, and passes when routed through an injectable
      seam such as `"${RM_CMD:-rm}"`. Verified by
      `python scripts/check_destructive_test_exec.py`.
- [ ] That gate runs in `make lint`, consistent with `check_raw_git_writes.py` and
      `check_wall_clock_asserts.py`. Verified by `make lint`.
- [ ] `HOME` is set to a non-existent path for the mutation subprocess so adjacent
      home-directory writes fail loudly. Verified by asserting the child's `HOME`.

## Testing

- `pytest tests/unit/test_mutation_sandbox.py` — enforcement (deny outside the
  allow-list, permit inside), fail-closed abort, and the opt-out WARNING.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_check_destructive_test_exec.py` — the lint gate flags an
  unguarded `subprocess`-exec of a destructive script and passes a seamed one.
- `make lint` — the new gate is wired and the tree is clean.
- `make typecheck` and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` — no new
  complexity or module-size violations.

## Definition of Done

- AC 4's enforcement test passes and fails correctly when the sandbox is disabled.
- AC 5's gate is in `make lint` with a covering test.
- No module-size violation: `mutation_gate.py` is **762 LOC against the 800 hard cap**,
  so the sandbox logic lands in its own module rather than inline.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the complexity ratchet stay green.
- Operator note documents the opt-out and its risk.

## Notes

Filed from the 2026-08-26 incident. The two other leaks found that day —
gate-snapshot accumulation (`a37c-d55c-72c3-439b`) and orphaned CPU load generators
(`f3d9-ecd8-df72-4fa1`) — are unrelated in cause and tracked separately.
